claims.claim: Opens in Algernon Moncrieff's morning-room flat in Half-Moon Street
claims.evidence: 'Morning-room in Algernon's flat in Half-Moon Street.'

claims.claim: Algernon plays piano while manservant Lane arranges tea
claims.evidence: 'The sound of a piano ... Lane is arranging afternoon tea'

claims.claim: Jack Worthing arrives, calling himself Ernest, to propose to Gwendolen
claims.evidence: 'Mr. Ernest Worthing.'; 'come up to town expressly to propose to'

claims.claim: In town Jack calls himself Ernest
claims.evidence: 'my name is Ernest in town and Jack in the country'

claims.claim: Algernon uses invalid friend Bunbury as excuse to leave town
claims.evidence: 'invaluable permanent invalid called Bunbury, in order that I may be able to go down into the country'

claims.claim: Lady Bracknell forbids it after learning Jack was found as a baby in a hand-bag
claims.evidence: 'I was in a hand-bag'; 'To be born, or at any rate bred, in a hand-bag'

claims.claim: Algernon poses as Jack's brother Ernest at Jack's country house
claims.evidence: 'Ask Mr. Ernest Worthing to come here'; 'my wicked cousin Ernest'

claims.claim: Algernon loves Jack's ward Cecily Cardew
claims.evidence: Act II Algernon and Cecily scene; 'an excessively pretty ward'

claims.claim: Both girls want only a man named Ernest
claims.evidence: 'my ideal has always been to love some one of the name of Ernest'

claims.claim: Miss Prism reveals she left a baby in a hand-bag

claims.evidence: 'Algernon's elder brother.'; 'Algy's elder brother! Then I have a brother after all'

claims.claim: His name is Ernest after all
Lady Bracknell is Algernon's aunt and Gwendolen's mother
claims.evidence: 'Aunt Augusta'; Gwendolen's mother in Act I
'when the Rector came in'; 'Rev. Canon Chasuble, D.D.'

claims.claim: Cecily is Jack's young ward; Jack is her guardian
claims.evidence: 'excessively pretty ward'; 'addresses me as her uncle'

claims.claim: Gwendolen Fairfax is Lady Bracknell's daughter, loved by Jack
